name: SOP Writer
summary: Turns a rough description of a recurring process into a step-by-step standard operating procedure.
description: Produces a numbered procedure with owners, inputs, decision points, and checks for each step, plus a short list of the ways the process usually goes wrong. It works only from what you describe and marks every assumption it had to make.
problems: Our processes live in one person's head
New hires keep doing recurring tasks differently
I need to document how we do things before we scale

inputs.label: Process description
inputs.description: How the process works today, in your own words. Messy is fine.
inputs.example: Every month-end, Priya exports invoices from the billing tool, checks them against the contracts sheet...

inputs.label: Roles involved
inputs.description: People or roles who take part, one per line.

outputs.label: Standard operating procedure
outputs.description: Purpose, scope, roles, numbered steps with owners and checks, and failure modes.

execution.system: You turn rough descriptions of recurring business processes into clear standard operating procedures. You work only from what the user describes. Anything you had to assume, such as an owner, a tool or a timing, goes in the assumptions list instead of being presented as fact.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.description: Why the process exists, in one or two sentences.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: When the procedure applies and when it does not.

action.description: What to do, starting with a verb.

owner.description: The role responsible for this step.

inputs.description: What the owner needs before starting.

decision.description: Any decision point and what to do in each case.

check.description: How to confirm the step was done correctly.

failure.description: How the process usually goes wrong.

prevention.description: How to prevent or catch it.

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: Everything not stated in the process description.

steps.name: Draft procedure
steps.responsibility: Write the SOP from the description and flag assumptions.
steps.prompt: Write the SOP as numbered steps in the order they happen. Give every step an owner role from the roles provided or described; if no owner is clear, pick the most plausible role and add that choice to the assumptions. Add a check to every step. List the two to five most likely failure modes.

steps.name: Check structure
steps.responsibility: Confirm every step has an owner, an action and a check.

steps.name: Review assumptions
steps.responsibility: Grade whether everything not in the description is listed as an assumption.

criteria.description: Every step names an owner role, an action and a check.
Anything not in the description is listed as an assumption.

review.rubric: Compare the SOP with the process description. Is every owner, tool, timing or rule that the description does not state listed under assumptions, rather than presented as fact? 5 = nothing unstated is presented as fact; 1 = many invented details.
